draft.title: Comparing two narratives
card: Comparing means putting two stories side by side. You look at how their forms, contexts and values are alike and different.
the type of text and how it is built, such as a diary, a film or a short story with one narrator.
the time, place and society in which a story was made. It can shape what a story shows.
Values are the beliefs a story invites you to hold, such as loyalty or freedom. A good comparison explains why a difference matters, not only what it is.
draft.remember: Do not only say how two stories differ. Explain why the difference matters.

a.q: Which sentence is the strongest comparison of two stories about leaving home?
opts: Letters show only one side, while a film shows many views
Story A is told as letters and Story B is a film
Story A is sad and Story B is also sad in places
Story A is better because its ending is more moving
a.why: The first option names a difference in form and explains what it does to the reader's view. The second only lists a difference, which is the tempting mistake. The others do not compare how the stories are made.
a.clue: Which one explains the effect of a difference?

b.q: Two stories about friendship were made decades apart in different countries. A student writes that they differ because they were made at different times. What would make this a stronger comparison?
opts: Explaining how each era's attitudes shaped its view of friendship
Adding the exact year each story was made
Saying that the first story is older and so is weaker
Retelling the plot of each story in more detail
b.why: Context matters when the student links the time and place to what the story shows. A date alone only states a fact. Judging a story weaker because it is older is not a comparison of why they differ.
b.clue: Link the setting of the story's making to what it shows.

The intended answer says letters show 'only' one side. That is an absolute claim the card does not support, and it is arguably false, since an epistolary story can include letters from several writers. A hedge such as 'often show one side' or 'can limit us to one side' would fix it.

proposal.title: Comparing two narratives
card: Comparing means putting two stories side by side. You look at how their forms, contexts and values are alike and different.
the type of text and how it is built, such as a diary, a film or a short story with one narrator. Form can change how close a reader feels to a character.
the time, place and society in which a story was made. It can shape what a story shows.
Values are the beliefs a story invites you to hold, such as loyalty or freedom. A good comparison explains why a difference matters, not only what it is.
proposal.remember: Do not only say how two stories differ. Explain why the difference matters.

a.q: Which sentence is the strongest comparison of two stories about leaving home?
opts: A's letters can feel more private to readers than B's film
Story A is told as letters and Story B is a film
Story A is sad and Story B is also sad in places
Story A is better because its ending is more moving
a.why: The sentence about the letters feeling more private names a difference in form and says what it can do for the reader, so it explains why the difference matters. Saying one story is letters and the other a film is the tempting choice, but it only lists the difference. The others note a likeness or give a personal judgement.
a.clue: Which one says what a difference does for the reader?

b.q: Two stories about friendship were made decades apart in different countries. A student writes that they differ because they were made at different times. What would make this a stronger comparison?
opts: Linking each era's attitudes to how it shows friendship
Adding the exact year each story was made
Saying the first story is weaker because it is older
Retelling the plot of each story in more detail
b.why: Context matters when the student links the time and place a story was made to what the story shows. Adding a date is tempting, but it only states another fact without explaining anything. Calling a story weaker because it is older is a judgement, not a reason for the difference.
b.clue: Think about what context can do to a story's ideas.
